Mitsubishi details CNC–humanoid work cell and human approval requirements

An interview explains Maisart planning, MCP/ROS communication and recovery limits; commercialization remains undecided.

Engineering.com ↗19 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Technical detail behind the JIMTOF demonstration

Engineering.com interviewed Mitsubishi Electric engineers about a work cell combining a Galaxea Dynamics humanoid, CNC equipment and an AI machining planner. A demonstrated workflow accepted spoken text for a tag, generated a program, loaded the workpiece, machined it and removed it. This is technical reporting on the demonstration, not a commercial work-cell launch.

The planner needs registered capabilities

Maisart technology supports planning and review. The planner communicates with the CNC through MCP and the robot through ROS. A registered library describes available motions, machine capabilities and supported workpieces; changes require library updates. The system therefore does not accept arbitrary production tasks without configuration.

Approval gates and recovery limitations

Human approval is required for actions such as starting machining, changing parameters and changing CNC settings. The system can retry a failed grasp, but alarms if a misplaced workpiece cannot enter the machine; automatic recovery remains in development. Mitsubishi is conducting validation research, envisages practical use around 2030 and has not decided commercialization plans.
